what_it_does: Graphify (PyPI 'graphifyy' 0.9.101, pinned commit 8e6a6d2) is a Python CLI plus an agent skill ('/graphify' in Claude Code, '$graphify' in Codex). It turns a folder of code, docs, PDFs, office files, images and audio/video into a NetworkX knowledge graph. Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter ASTs, no LLM needed. Docs and media get a semantic pass from host-agent subagents or a configured API backend. It writes graphify-out/graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md (god nodes, communities, surprising links, suggested questions), graph.html, an optional --wiki export (index.md plus one article per community or god node), and Obsidian, Neo4j, FalkorDB and GraphML exports. An optional MCP server serves the graph. Agents query it with 'graphify query/path/explain' instead of grep and read. It also installs agent-steering parts: always-on rule blocks in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or GEMINI.md, PreToolUse nudge or deny hooks, and git hooks that rebuild the graph after commit, checkout, merge and rewrite. On the user's premise: it is NOT vector retrieval. README.md:38 says "No embeddings, no vector store". Querying is lexical token matching followed by graph traversal. It is a structural 'data map' of what exists where and how it connects. It is not a store of curated project knowledge (why decisions were made).
mechanism:
Verified in source, not only from the README.

(1) Pipeline: detect.py classifies files, honors .gitignore and .graphifyignore, and silently skips secret-bearing files (.env, .pem, id_rsa, .netrc, .npmrc, .pypirc, .git-credentials; detect.py:134-145). extract.py (11.9k lines) does tree-sitter AST extraction across about 40 languages. Edges are tagged EXTRACTED, INFERRED or AMBIGUOUS. For non-code files, skill.md Step B dispatches parallel subagents with references/extraction-spec.md as the prompt. This uses the Agent tool on Claude and spawn_agent with multi_agent=true on Codex (skill-codex.md:276-283). Headless 'graphify extract' calls an API backend instead (llm.py BACKENDS: Gemini, Kimi, Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama, or claude-cli via 'claude -p'). Results are cached per file under graphify-out/cache/. The AST cache is namespaced by package, schema and grammar version. The semantic cache is keyed by content plus a prompt fingerprint (cache.py:22-35, 139-163). dedup.py (minhash and rapidfuzz) merges entities. cluster.py runs Leiden (graspologic) or falls back to networkx Louvain. Communities get names from an LLM, or hub-derived names when none is available. Labeling falls back to the 'claude -p' CLI (Opus by default) when no API key is set (llm.py:3936-3949).

(2) Storage, project: graphify-out/{graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.html, cache/, cache/hook_sessions/, wiki/, memory/, reflections/LESSONS.md, .graphify_python, .graphify_root}.

(3) Storage, outside the project: ~/.claude/skills/graphify/ and a registration block in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (default 'graphify install'; install.py:260, 993-1003). Also ~/.codex/skills/graphify (install.py:648), ~/.cache/graphify/skill-locks (install.py:62), ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log (hooks.py:365), ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> for GitHub URL clones (cli.py:1438), ~/.graphify/global-graph.json (global_graph.py:10), ~/.graphify/providers.json (llm.py:266), and the opt-in ~/.cache/graphify-queries.log (querylog.py:15-31). Git side: .git/hooks or core.hooksPath, plus a merge.graphify.* git config entry and a .gitattributes line (hooks.py:1004-1050).

(4) Retrieval: serve.py _score_nodes (line 569) tokenizes the question and scores node labels, source paths and attributes. references/query.md:25 states it is case-folded substring plus IDF, with "no stemming, no synonyms, no cross-language match". The skill makes the agent expand the query against the graph's vocabulary first. Seeds then go through _bfs or _dfs (lines 1067 and 1098) to a set depth. _subgraph_to_text (line 1125) renders within a token budget (default 2000, about 3 chars per token), never cuts seed nodes, and prints an over-budget notice. 'path' runs a shortest path and reports the confidence of its weakest hop. Exit codes are 0 for an answer, 3 for an ambiguous name (candidates listed), 4 for no match. No embedding library is imported anywhere in graphify/*.py.

(5) Wiki export: wiki.py to_wiki builds Markdown purely from graph structure. Each article lists top nodes by degree, cross-community links, source files and a confidence audit trail. to_wiki owns its output directory and deletes every *.md it did not produce in that run (wiki.py:356-363, 461-477).

(6) Feedback memory: 'graphify save-result' writes Q&A docs to graphify-out/memory/. reflect.py turns their outcomes (useful, dead_end, corrected) into reflections/LESSONS.md using a time-decayed score: 30-day half-life, and at least 2 corroborating results before a node is 'preferred' (reflect.py:51-52).

(7) Agent steering: 'graphify claude install' writes PreToolUse hooks into .claude/settings.json: matcher Bash|Grep runs 'graphify hook-guard search' and Read|Glob runs 'graphify hook-guard read', with timeout 10 (install.py:506-511, 2241-2263). The guard (cli.py:1169+) reads the tool JSON on stdin, parses Bash tokens so quoted prose does not count as a search, and emits an additionalContext nudge, at most 5 per session (cli.py:1004). In --strict mode it denies the first in-project Read per session. It fails open. Codex gets an intentionally no-op 'hook-check' hook (install.py:1908-1950) and relies on the AGENTS.md block. Git hooks start a detached, AST-only rebuild (hooks.py:363-380; watch.py:2166 says "No LLM needed"), with a 600s timeout and a GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK opt-out.

(8) MCP: serve.py runs over stdio by default, or Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8080 with an optional --api-key (serve.py:3404-3412). Tools: query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, shortest_path, list_prs, get_pr_impact, triage_prs. graphify install does not write any MCP config.

hosts.claude_code: Supported as a user- or project-scope skill plus hooks. There is no .claude-plugin manifest, so it is not a Claude Code plugin. 'graphify install' copies graphify/skill.md to ~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md (with references/) and adds a '# graphify' registration block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. 'graphify claude install' (or 'install --project') writes a '## graphify' always-on block into the project CLAUDE.md and PreToolUse hooks into .claude/settings.json (Bash|Grep and Read|Glob; strict mode can deny the first raw Read). The skill has no disable-model-invocation, so the model can trigger it on its own. Semantic extraction relies on Agent-tool subagents.
hosts.codex: Supported through the instruction file only. 'graphify install --platform codex' copies skill-codex.md to ~/.codex/skills/graphify/SKILL.md (or .codex/skills with --project; install.py:646-650), adds an always-on section to AGENTS.md, and registers a deliberately no-op PreToolUse 'hook-check' in .codex/hooks.json, because Codex Desktop rejects additionalContext (install.py:1946-1948). Parallel extraction needs 'multi_agent = true' in ~/.codex/config.toml and spawn_agent; it is invoked as $graphify. Unknown: whether the current Codex discovers .codex/skills, since OAW installs Codex skills into .agents/skills ('--platform agents' writes there instead). Behavior differs by host: Claude gets runtime hooks, Codex only gets prose rules.
hosts.other: 20+ other hosts through per-host skill variants and rule files: Gemini CLI (BeforeTool hook), CodeBuddy (PreToolUse), Pi and Oh My Pi (native TS extension calling hook-guard), Cursor rules, Kiro steering, VS Code Copilot, Copilot CLI, Aider, OpenCode, Kilo, Amp, Droid, Trae, Hermes, Devin, Antigravity, and the generic Agent Skills layout (~/.agents/skills). There is also an optional MCP server (stdio, or HTTP via the Dockerfile) that any MCP client can attach to by hand.

runtime_requirements: Python >=3.10, installed via uv tool, pipx or pip as PyPI 'graphifyy' (double y; a single-y 'graphify' is an unrelated package)

Core non-stdlib dependencies (pyproject.toml:14-54): networkx>=3.4, numpy, rapidfuzz, pyyaml, tomli (<3.11), tree-sitter>=0.25,<0.26, plus about 25 native tree-sitter grammar wheels (python, js, ts, go, rust, java, c, cpp, c#, kotlin, swift, php, ruby, etc.)

Optional extras: mcp/starlette/anyio/uvicorn (MCP server), watchdog (watch), graspologic or graspologic-native (Leiden), pypdf/markdownify, python-docx/openpyxl, faster-whisper/av/yt-dlp (video), neo4j, falkordb, psycopg + tree-sitter-sql (Postgres), openai/anthropic/boto3/tiktoken (LLM backends), jieba (Chinese query segmentation), matplotlib/pillow (SVG)

An LLM for the non-code semantic pass and community naming: host-agent subagents (Claude Agent tool, Codex spawn_agent) or API keys (GEMINI/GOOGLE, MOONSHOT/Kimi, ANTHROPIC, OPENAI, DEEPSEEK, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Ollama) or the 'claude -p' CLI. With no key set, the backend is auto-detected from ambient environment keys. A code-only AST graph needs none of this
git (hooks, merge driver, clone of GitHub URLs) and gh CLI (graphify prs)
Optional external services: Neo4j, FalkorDB, PostgreSQL

No persistent daemon by default. Optional foreground 'graphify watch'. Optional long-running MCP server (stdio, or HTTP 127.0.0.1:8080). Git hooks spawn detached short-lived rebuild processes per commit, checkout, merge or rewrite
A browser to view graph.html, which loads vis-network@9.1.6 from unpkg; callflow HTML loads mermaid@11 from jsDelivr with a floating major version

gates.evidence: pyproject.toml:10-11 license = "Apache-2.0", license-files = [LICENSE, LICENSE-MIT, NOTICE]. NOTICE says pre-relicense contributions remain under MIT. Redistributable; any copied method or file must keep LICENSE and NOTICE and mark modifications (plan line 75).

graphify/skill.md frontmatter is valid (name 'graphify', description 353 chars) but the body is 48,061 bytes LF-normalized (49,252 on disk with CRLF), about twice the 24,000-byte gate. Codex variant: 48,821 B; windows: 50,457 B. Plus about 49 KB of on-demand references in graphify/skills/claude/references/. The skill also lives at graphify/skill.md and is copied by an installer, rather than shipping as a standard <name>/SKILL.md package.

(a) PreToolUse hooks on the 4 highest-frequency tools: install.py:506-511 (Bash|Grep -> hook-guard search, Read|Glob -> hook-guard read, timeout 10); strict mode denies the first Read (cli.py:1169-1186 docstring). (b) The skill auto-installs packages without asking: skill.md:92 'uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy', skill.md:97 'pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages'. (c) Always-on block: 'put this rule in every subagent prompt' (always_on/claude-md.md:6) and 'Do not flag it as churn or suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks' (always_on/claude-md.md:10, agents-md.md:13). (d) Git hooks start detached processes (hooks.py:363-380) and add a merge driver and .gitattributes entry (hooks.py:1004-1050). (e) A repo-controlled interpreter path runs as code: query.md:14 runs '$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c ...' on the fast path, which skips Step 1, the step that rewrites that file (skill.md:57). The git hook falls back to the same file (hooks.py:41-52). (f) Model spend without an explicit choice: labeling falls back to 'claude -p' (llm.py:3936-3949), and the backend is picked from ambient API keys, Gemini first (llm.py:3544-3548); Kimi routes to China (README.md:435). Every item is a flag for a human to judge, not an automatic rejection.

No telemetry or analytics SDK and no update check found in graphify/*.py. Network use: LLM backend SDKs (llm.py:145-210 base_urls); SSRF-guarded fetch for 'graphify add <url>' (security.py:195-291); 'git clone --depth 1' of GitHub URLs into ~/.graphify/repos (cli.py:1438-1455); gh CLI (prs.py:144); CDN scripts in generated HTML (exporters/html.py:733 unpkg vis-network@9.1.6; callflow_html.py:1708 jsdelivr mermaid@11). Upsell links printed to app.graphify.com (cli.py:142, install.py:1025, __main__.py:1096). The query log is opt-in in code (querylog.py:15-31), but README.md:437 says queries are logged by default (doc/code mismatch).

Default 'graphify install' writes ~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md (install.py:260) and edits ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (install.py:999-1003). It always writes ~/.cache/graphify/skill-locks/*.lock (install.py:62), even with --project. Git hooks log to ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log (hooks.py:365, 544). Clones go to ~/.graphify/repos (cli.py:1438), the global graph to ~/.graphify/global-graph.json (global_graph.py:10-12), providers to ~/.graphify/providers.json (llm.py:266). The merge driver goes into git config (hooks.py:1026-1027). '--project' limits the skill and hooks to the repo, but not the locks or logs.

pyproject.toml:14-54: networkx, numpy, rapidfuzz, pyyaml, tree-sitter plus about 25 native grammar wheels are required at runtime. OAW's runtime rule is Python 3.10+ standard library only (oaw-ref/AGENTS.md: 'keep runtime dependencies in the standard library'). It can never be vendored into the OAW runtime; at most it could be referenced as an externally installed tool, like the EGM plugin precedent.

Partial overlap with native features. Claude Code and Codex already do agentic grep, glob and read exploration (and Claude Code has Explore subagents and LSP-backed navigation through plugins; this is unverified at the current host version). Neither host natively keeps a persisted, multi-language structural graph with communities, god nodes or path queries; that part is new. The project's own evidence that it beats native search is small: BENCHMARKS.md:145-147 reports ERPNext n=6, key-fact coverage 70.8% to 82.0% at about 140K tokens per query, and the harness (crosstool/run.py, memory/runner.py) is not in this repo (git ls-files shows none), so it cannot be reproduced at this SHA. BENCHMARKS.md:183 mentions 'a local embedder', which contradicts README.md:38.

It does not fill the same capability slot as OAW LLM Wiki (oaw-ref/README.md:81: wiki_sync.py renders curated docs/raw notes into docs/knowledge with metadata, link, freshness and orphan lint, and annotations). graphify's wiki is generated from graph structure, owns and sweeps its directory (wiki.py:356-363, 461-477), and has no frontmatter provenance, freshness lint or annotation preservation. It overlaps in part with: context_hub search/recall (graphify query), memory promotion (save-result/reflect LESSONS.md vs wiki_sync promote_candidates), egm-drift-report (code vs docs), and the AGENTS.md policy (always-on block). The capability OAW lacks is a structural code map; this slot is empty in OAW, so the tool could only enter a pack.

Both hosts are first-class targets: Claude (skill.md, CLAUDE.md, PreToolUse hooks) and Codex (skill-codex.md, AGENTS.md, no-op hook-check; install.py:646-650, 1908-1950), generated from one source by tools/skillgen/platforms.toml. Caveat: enforcement differs (runtime hooks on Claude, prose only on Codex). The Codex skill path is .codex/skills, while OAW uses .agents/skills; whether current Codex discovers it is unknown.

Every invocation loads a 48 KB body (about 12K tokens), plus references (query.md etc., about 49 KB total) on demand. A 353-char model-invocable description is always loaded. If installed, the always-on CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block is about 1.2-1.5 KB per session, and hooks inject additionalContext nudges up to 5 per session (cli.py:1004, GRAPHIFY_HOOK_NUDGE_CAP default 5). The full build dispatches about ceil(non-code files/22) extraction subagents (skill.md:225-229). This would blow any reasonable core budget and probably a pack budget too, unless the skill is trimmed.

skill.md:3 description: 'Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists'. There is no disable-model-invocation, so it competes with oaw-evidence (why/decision questions), oaw-wiki (project content), egm-drift-report and native exploration. The always-on rule further forces 'graphify query before your first grep, search or source-file read' (always_on/claude-md.md:6). Needs the trigger test set.

always_on/claude-md.md:6 adds a mandatory query-first router and makes the agent copy it into every subagent prompt. That conflicts with OAW's native-first rule 'No router, no mandatory startup reads' (oaw-ref/README.md:78, 141). claude-md.md:10 ('Do not flag it as churn or suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks') muzzles EGM and goldfish reviewers. skill.md:92-97 auto-installs, which conflicts with 'never auto-install or auto-apply' (plan line 68, 430). agents-md.md:9 ('dirty graph files are not a reason to skip graphify') conflicts with OAW's 'evidence, not instructions; check against current code'. skill.md:223 says 'MANDATORY: You MUST use the Agent tool'.

oaw_overlap:
Short answer to the user's premise: graphify cannot replace the OAW LLM wiki. It is not vectorization either: README.md:38 and query.md:25 confirm lexical substring+IDF seeding plus BFS/DFS traversal, with no embeddings.

(1) oaw-wiki / wiki_sync.py (raw -> knowledge). The two answer different questions. OAW's wiki compiles human- or agent-written source notes (source_id, title, topic_id, summary, last_updated) into topic pages. It keeps provenance per source, preserves AI annotations across rebuilds, and lints for broken links, missing metadata, stale pages (raw newer than page), orphaned or duplicated sources and placeholders. It is curated 'why/what we decided' knowledge, deterministic and stdlib-only. graphify --wiki is generated from code structure: community and god-node articles listing degree-ranked node names, source files and an EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail. Its labels come from an LLM or hubs. It owns its directory and deletes any .md it did not produce, so pointed at docs/knowledge it would erase OAW pages and annotations. It has no freshness or metadata lint and no claim-level provenance, and it cannot represent decisions, superseded conclusions or contradictions. Its rationale coverage is limited to '# WHY:'/'# NOTE:' comments and ADR references pulled from code, plus LLM extraction from docs. Verdict: complementary 'where/how-connected' layer, not a replacement.

(2) context_hub.py search / memory recall. Both are lexical. OAW's is a plain case-insensitive substring search over knowledge pages and memory, with bounded, cited excerpts and a cursor. graphify adds IDF scoring, graph expansion, a seed-preserving token budget and ambiguity exit codes. For code-structure questions graphify should retrieve better; for decision and evidence questions it has no data. Neither does cross-language matching (graphify needs agent-side expansion or the jieba extra for Chinese).

(3) Memory promotion. graphify save-result/reflect (time-decayed outcome scoring, corroboration threshold, contested and dead-end categories) overlaps with .agents/memory.md plus wiki_sync promote_candidates (tier plus citation counts).

(4) AGENTS.md policy. graphify's always-on block would inject a second router into the short, OAW-managed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. That conflicts with native-first and could make 'oaw.py doctor' report managed-file drift (unverified).

(5) egm-drift-report. Partial overlap (code vs docs drift) through graphify's affected/PR-impact features.

(6) improvement.py and the catalog plan. No overlap; graphify has its own skillgen/check, similar in spirit to sync_examples.py.

Net: the empty OAW capability slot is a 'structural code map'. The LLM-wiki slot is not contested.
integration_rationale:
Following the plan's preference order (plan lines 131-137):

(a) Replace the LLM wiki: reject. It is a different capability (structural map vs curated rationale with provenance and lint), and its wiki exporter deletes files it does not own.

(b) Swallow whole as core: impossible. Non-stdlib native deps fail the stdlib gate; the 48 KB body fails the 24,000 B structure gate; always-on routing and 'do not flag' rules conflict with native-first; hooks, git hooks, writes to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and auto-install violate never-auto-install and the host-owns-permissions rule.

(c) Pack: OAW does lack a code-map capability and the tool covers both hosts, so a future 'code-map' pack is conceivable. Precedent: EGM is recorded as an official external install pinned to a version, not vendored. That route is only open if the pack (1) disables the always-on blocks and PreToolUse hooks, (2) lets users invoke the skill manually only, or trims it under 24 KB with references, and (3) passes the paid A/B and the 'diarrhea' integration checks. The user's own benchmark (n=6, about 140K tokens per query, harness not in repo) is not evidence. Until then any packaging decision is needs_ab_first, and users who want it today should run it local_only at project scope without --strict.

(d) What OAW can safely take now, stdlib-only and without new skills, is graphify's methods, in wiki_sync.py, context_hub.py and the catalog digest process; see nutrients. Each absorbed change still goes through improvement.py, with matched A/B evidence before accept, and is cited per version (Apache-2.0 attribution).

Note: star count (141k in 7 months) was ignored; the decision rests on code.
nutrients: Edge and claim confidence tags (EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS, wiki.py audit trail). wiki_sync could mark each compiled statement or link as quoted from source vs inferred, and lint could report an AMBIGUOUS/INFERRED ratio per topic page. Stdlib-only.

Budgeted retrieval rendering (serve.py:1125-1305): never cut the seed or direct hits, render nodes before edges, and when over budget print the smallest budget that would fit instead of truncating silently. Fits context_hub memory recall --max-chars and search --compact.

Ambiguity refusal with scriptable exit codes (0 answer, 3 ambiguous with candidate list, 4 no match; README 'Using the graph directly'). Fits context_hub get/search so agents and scripts never guess a topic.

Rationale harvesting: graphify turns '# WHY:' / '# NOTE:' comments and ADR/RFC citations into nodes linked to code. A stdlib regex pass in wiki_sync could emit them as docs/raw source notes with file:line provenance, so they get OAW's existing lint, freshness and annotation handling. This links the code map to the 'why' layer without a graph database.

Optional stdlib 'code map' raw source: a Python-only pass with the stdlib ast module (module -> imports, defs, callers) could write a deterministic docs/raw/_codemap note. It would be rendered and linted by wiki_sync, giving a minimal 'data map' with no tree-sitter dependency. Must be A/B-tested before adoption.

Outcome-scored promotion (reflect.py:1-24, 51-52): signed, time-decayed scores (30-day half-life) from useful / dead_end / corrected outcomes, a minimum of 2 distinct corroborations before 'preferred', plus explicit 'contested' and 'known dead ends' sections. Could improve wiki_sync promote_candidates, which today uses tier plus citation count, and fits OAW's 'evidence, not instructions' principle.

Content-hash plus renderer-version staleness (cache.py:22-35, 139-163): record a source content hash and the renderer version in compiled page metadata. lint then flags staleness by hash, not only by last_updated date, and a renderer upgrade invalidates outputs deterministically.

Write-if-changed and end-of-run orphan sweep (wiki.py write_text_atomic_if_changed; sweep after the produced set is known): avoids rewrite churn and an empty-directory window during wiki_sync build. It must still never delete files the tool does not own, which OAW already enforces.

Sensitive-file exclusion list (detect.py:134-145: .env*, *.pem/key/p12, id_rsa*, .netrc/.npmrc/.pypirc/.git-credentials/.boto, keeping .env.example templates). wiki_sync and context_hub could refuse to compile or return such files from docs/raw.

Hook engineering lessons for the planned oaw-digest-monitor mod or any future OAW hook (install.py:478-511; cli.py:994-1186; hooks.py:340-470): fail open, explicit short timeout (10s, not the host's 600s default), parse executed shell tokens rather than substrings (no false hits on quoted prose or heredocs), a per-session nudge cap, never strand an agent (a deny fires at most once per session), worktree guard, an env-var opt-out, and printing which file a symlinked CLAUDE.md actually points to.

Single-source multi-host skill generation with a drift check (tools/skillgen/gen.py --check in pre-commit) and progressive-disclosure references/ per host. OAW already has sync_examples.py; borrow the references split as the standard way to keep SKILL bodies under the 24,000 B gate.

Query expansion step (query.md Step 0): before a lexical search, expand the user's wording against the corpus's own vocabulary without inventing terms. Worth adding to the oaw-evidence skill text for Traditional Chinese questions against English notes and code. Prompt-only, no dependency.
diarrhea_risks: Trigger theft: graphify's description ('any question about a codebase ... or project content', skill.md:3) and the always-on 'query before your first grep/read' rule would pull 'why did we decide X' questions away from oaw-evidence and oaw-wiki toward a graph that holds no decision data.

Instruction conflict with native-first: a second mandatory router copied into every subagent prompt (always_on/claude-md.md:6) contradicts OAW's 'No router, no mandatory startup reads' and inflates every EGM subagent prompt.

Reviewer muzzling: 'Do not flag it as churn or suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks' (claude-md.md:10) could suppress legitimate EGM review and goldfish findings, a regression in the design-review pack.

Hook latency and noise: PreToolUse guards on Bash|Grep|Read|Glob spawn a Python process on every call (the code itself cites about 170ms warm, install.py:500-502) and inject up to 5 nudges per session. --strict denies the first Read, which can break harness_check and EGM flows. Codex gets no hook, so behavior diverges between hosts.

Context blowup: the 48 KB skill body (about 12K tokens per invocation) plus references; doc extraction fans out to N subagents; the project's own figure is about 140K tokens per query on ERPNext. This contradicts the OAW goal of spending tokens on reasoning.
Data loss: pointing graphify --wiki at docs/knowledge, or any OAW-owned directory, deletes every .md it did not produce (wiki.py:461-477), including OAW topic pages and AI annotations.

Lifecycle conflicts: it edits CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and .claude/settings.json, plus git hooks, git config merge driver and .gitattributes, outside OAW's managed-file hashes. Likely 'doctor' drift and 'migrate' conflicts (unverified). Detached rebuild processes conflict with the 'no background daemons' rule.

Unconsented install and spend: the skill runs 'pip install ... --break-system-packages' or 'uv tool install --upgrade' (skill.md:92-97). Labeling falls back to 'claude -p' (Opus by default), and the backend auto-detects from ambient keys (Gemini first, Kimi to China), so docs can leave the machine without an explicit choice.

Repo-controlled execution: the query fast path runs '$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)' (query.md:14) without first rewriting it. A cloned repo with a committed graphify-out/ can name an arbitrary executable. Plausible and low-probability, but real for untrusted repos.

Expectation mismatch: the user expects vectorized semantic recall, but matching is lexical (query.md:25). Chinese questions against English labels miss unless the agent expands the query or the jieba extra is installed. A stale graph is trusted first when hooks are absent.

Supply chain: PyPI name 'graphifyy' vs typo 'graphify'; about 25 native tree-sitter wheels; a floating mermaid@11 CDN script; 0.9.x releases daily (fast churn makes pinned-SHA evidence go stale quickly).

Documentation drift reduces trust: README.md:437 says queries are logged by default while querylog.py:16-31 is opt-in; BENCHMARKS.md:183 cites 'a local embedder' while README.md:38 says no embeddings.
proposed_ab_tests: Code-map behavior A/B (both hosts, 5 repeats, pre-registered tolerance). A = native host; B = native + graphify official install (project scope, nudge hooks, no strict); C = OAW core + graphify manual-only (no hooks, no always-on block). Fixtures: the OAW repo plus one mid-size polyglot repo (about 50-200k LOC). 20 questions (where-is, what-calls, cross-file path, architecture overview), each with required and forbidden key-fact assertions. Measure: key-fact pass counts, total tokens including graph build and extraction subagents, wall time, tool calls, raw files read. Pass needs C >= B (parity) and C > A to justify any pack.

LLM-wiki replacement A/B, which directly tests the user's premise. Fixture: a repo with docs/raw -> docs/knowledge holding decisions, superseded decisions and one planted contradiction. Arms: OAW wiki + memory recall; graphify (--wiki + query, docs semantic pass); both. 15 'why / what was decided / is this still current' questions plus 5 structure questions. Measure: correct decision recall, superseded-decision detection, citation accuracy (file:line), contradiction surfacing, tokens. Expectation to verify: OAW wins on rationale, graphify on structure, and 'both' is at least as good as the best single arm with no regressions.

Integration (diarrhea) suite: install graphify alongside OAW core plus the design-review pack. Re-run the full catalog regression (EGM 30 scenarios, oaw-evidence, oaw-wiki and oaw-improve cases) with and without graphify. Measure per-scenario pass-count deltas within the frozen tolerance; any regression means reject.

Trigger test set: 40 labeled prompts (structure vs rationale vs wiki maintenance vs drift vs none) in English and Traditional Chinese. Measure the mis-trigger rate with and without graphify's description and always-on block, on both hosts.

Context and latency budget: startup metadata token delta (descriptions plus always-on block), per-session hook additionalContext tokens, p50/p95 added latency per Bash/Grep/Read/Glob call with hooks on (Windows and POSIX), and per-invocation skill tokens (48 KB body).

Cost break-even: graph build cost on a doc-heavy repo (subagent extraction tokens, or API spend with --backend pinned) vs per-query savings over N queries compared with the native baseline. Record whether any 'claude -p' or auto-detected backend spend happened without explicit consent.

Chinese query recall: 20 Traditional Chinese questions against an English-labeled graph. Compare hit rate without expansion, with the skill's vocabulary-expansion step, and with the jieba extra; compare to context_hub recall on the same corpus.

Strict-mode safety test (fixture only, no paid run needed): verify that --strict never blocks OAW harness_check, EGM review-loop or migrate flows, and that GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1 and uninstall fully restore .claude/settings.json, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, git hooks and .gitattributes byte-for-byte.
claims_to_verify: graphify/skill.md is 48,455 bytes at HEAD (LF), with a 48,061-byte body after frontmatter (49,252 bytes on disk with CRLF). That exceeds the 24,000-byte structure gate. Its frontmatter has no disable-model-invocation, and the description begins 'Use for any question about a codebase'.

Retrieval is not vector-based: README.md:38 says 'No embeddings, no vector store'. graphify/skills/claude/references/query.md:25 says the query CLI matches by 'case-folded substring + IDF' with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language match. serve.py implements _score_nodes (line 569), _bfs (1067), _dfs (1098) and token-budgeted _subgraph_to_text (1125). No embedding library is imported anywhere in graphify/*.py.

'graphify claude install' writes PreToolUse hooks into .claude/settings.json with matchers 'Bash|Grep' -> 'graphify hook-guard search' and 'Read|Glob' -> 'graphify hook-guard read', timeout 10 (install.py:506-511, 2241-2263). --strict makes the read guard deny the first in-project raw Read per session (cli.py:1169-1186).

always_on/claude-md.md:6 tells the agent to run 'graphify query' before the first grep, search or source-file read and to put that rule in every subagent prompt. Line 10 says 'Do not flag it as churn or suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks'.
skill.md Step 1 installs the package without asking: line 92 'uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy', line 97 'pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages'.
The core runtime dependencies in pyproject.toml:14-54 are non-stdlib: networkx, numpy, rapidfuzz, pyyaml, tree-sitter 0.25 and about 25 tree-sitter grammar packages.

wiki.py to_wiki owns its output directory and deletes any *.md it did not produce in that run (wiki.py:356-363, 461-477). Community labeling falls back to the 'claude -p' CLI when no API key is set (llm.py:3936-3949).

querylog.py:15-31 logs queries only when GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG or GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_ENABLE is set, contradicting README.md:437, which says every query is logged to ~/.cache/graphify-queries.log by default. The git hooks log detached rebuilds to ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log (hooks.py:365).
